newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell says no oil stoppage after Nigeria deadline.
newsitem.headline: Shell says no oil stoppage after Nigeria deadline.

text.p: The Nigerian unit of oil giant Royal Dutch Shell Group said on Wednesday that its oil activities were proceeding normally after an ultimatum by four oil-producing communities to pay compensation or leave expired.
"We have no reports of any disruptions or delays in Burutu," a Shell spokesman said in Lagos, adding "There is no immediate threat to our operations."

The Niger Delta Oil-Producing Development Organisation said on Tuesday that its president, Matthew Eregbeng, had been arrested by state security operatives before the expiry of the July 8 deadline and blamed the action on Shell.
"We have not been informed of any arrest. We are not involved in any arrest," Shell's western division general manager Joshua Udofia said.

The four ethnic Ijaw communities in the Burutu local government of Delta state had told Shell to leave or be forced out of the area where Shell has two flow stations. Each flow station pumps between 20,000-30,000 barrels per day.

Shell Nigeria, a joint venture between the Shell group and state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp, is the biggest operator in the West African country and pumps about half the national output of roughly two million bpd.
It has dozens of staff in the Burutu area and two local policemen armed only with pistols.
"We don't work behind guns. We don't have mobile police," said Udofia.
Industry sources said Shell executives met community leaders and the local state military administrator on Tuesday over the ultimatum but did not reveal the outcome of the talks.

The four communities involved recently won a tussle against Shell in local courts over compensation of around 30 million naira ($353,000) for environmental damage, but say Shell is now planning to appeal to a higher court.
Shell says no compensation can be paid for the 1982 oil spill, from the trans-Forcados pipeline, because it was found to have been caused by sabotage.
The company also says it cleared up the spilled oil and that it is exercising its right of appeal by contesting the verdict.

Ethnic clashes in March between Ijaw and Itsekiri tribesmen in the Warri area killed scores of people and forced Shell to close several oil wells earlier this year after fighting erupted over the relocation of a local government headquarters.
